rationale: mpeg2dec is a media decoder dominated by hot inner loops (VLC bitstream parsing, IDCT, motion compensation) and a small, tight binary with no debug profile available, so the weight table favors low-cost, low-risk transformations and throttles the expensive ones. SUB gets high weights across dimensions because arithmetic substitution is cheap at runtime and in size and preserves correctness, making it ideal for saturating hot loops without measurable decode slowdown. SPLIT is similarly favored (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights) since block splitting adds static-analysis friction with negligible overhead, though its standalone security is modest. FLA and BCF carry elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties: flattening the decode loops or injecting bogus predicates into IDCT/VLC inner loops would inflate runtime substantially for a codec, so SecurityGain stays moderate and cost dimensions high so the selection is confined to cold functions (setup, error handling). IBR and ICALL are kept moderately enabled — they are effective against static RE of the dispatch table and function-call graph, with acceptable indirect-branch overhead for a decoder whose call graph is not extremely hot — while IGV is allowed mildly since the C benchmark has limited global-variable indirection opportunity. All seven passes remain considered rather than disabled, letting the feature-driven selector suppress them per-function where profile evidence (e.g., loop-dominated code) makes their cost dimensions dominate.
